newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA MUSEUM SHOWS CEAUSESCU HUNTING TROPHIES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA MUSEUM SHOWS CEAUSESCU HUNTING TROPHIES.

text.p: Hunting trophies bagged by Romania's executed dictator Nicolae Ceausescu went on display for the first time on Wednesday at a museum north of Bucharest, the state news agency Rompres said.
The agency said up to 4,000 trophies were on show in the museum, housed in a castle in the Carpathian mountains belonging to a family of aristocrats now living in Britain.
The prizes, it said, included a mountain goat considered a world record catch in 1934 in terms of its size and appearance and unmatched since.
Ceausescu accorded himself exclusive bear hunting rights during his 24-year term in office on personal reserves of prime forest totalling 600,000 hectares (1.5 million acres).

Pictures of Ceausescu, his wife Elena and other Communist party members pointing proudly to dozens of boars shot on hunting expeditions stunned downtrodden Romanians after the December 1989 upheaval which ousted him.

A government report from 1991 said that the Communist Party had amassed more than 730 million dollars in cash, property and treasures during Ceausescu's rule, including 21 palaces, 41 villas and 20 hunting lodges.
